business_rules.statement: The integration surface is closed at the first version. Adding an integration is a scope decision taken by the client, never an engineering convenience.
business_rules.enforcement_point: release planning and the deny-by-default egress allow-list

business_rules.statement: No integration may weaken a platform floor. Tenants may make the platform stricter than default and may never make it looser; the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value rather than logging it.
No integration participates in the deviation-triggering path. No external system and no AI service may sit between a measurement and its severity classification.

Fallback safety priority order: worker safety, tenant isolation, security, authorization, qualification, specification and evaluation controls, approval and release authority, data integrity, auditability, controlled continuity, clear user communication, recovery and reconciliation.
Controlled continuity sits ninth, below data integrity and auditability: keeping going is less important than keeping the record true.

No fallback may bypass RBAC, cross tenants, bypass qualification, specifications, evaluation, approval, publication, or Severity 1 hold and release rules; nor silently discard or overwrite data; nor present stale data as current; nor present failure as success; nor depend indefinitely on one person; nor enter an infinite retry loop.

A connection is an integration when it crosses the platform boundary, the far side is operated by someone other than the AVIIXA runtime, and a far-side failure changes what a user of one of the five surfaces experiences.
Every integration names exactly one owning surface; where a failure is experienced on several surfaces the owning surface is the one that holds the record, which is the Delivery Operations Hub.
Authentication is not authorization. Role assignment stays inside the platform; an assertion carrying a group or role claim is untrusted input, logged and ignored.
No directory provisioning means account lifecycle stays manual. Departure is a two-step act: reassign active and upcoming runs, then archive. SSO removes the credential, not the record.
Platform and tenant roles are separate security domains; a Tenant Admin has no platform authority; a tenant-federated identity provider can never yield a platform console session.

The platform maps the asserted subject to exactly one existing platform user record within exactly one tenant; where no such record exists, sign-in is refused, because there is no just-in-time provisioning at the first version.
A notification is never the only mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, qualification, authorization, approval, suspension, or a device command. Email is the escalation's carrier, never its enforcement.
Sending is not delivery, delivery is not opening, opening is not acknowledgement, and acknowledgement is not the business action. No surface may collapse these states.

External notification recipients and quiet hours are outside the first version. A tenant cannot direct AVIIXA email to a distribution list outside its own user records except the named tenant contact address.
Learning on the platform is memory accumulation, not fine-tuning, and is model-agnostic by construction; no platform behaviour may depend on the identity of a specific model.

No AI model sits in the deviation-triggering path; detection is rule-based on the worker's device using version-pinned limits and severity mappings; agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.
The evaluation gate binds everything including the root: no agent, capability or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios; the gate is hard, always, for every tenant.

AI is advisory unless the source explicitly grants execution authority. It may never elevate permissions, change tenant scope, impersonate a role, self-approve, release a Severity 1 hold, bypass a gate, classify deviations, execute stale queued actions, or delete evidence or audit history.
A tenant's manufacturing memory is isolated to that tenant: nothing is shared with another tenant, and nothing is used as external training data.
business_rules.enforcement_point: compute vendor contract and memory stores

business_rules.statement: Emergency pause renders as unavailability, never silence; in-flight agent runs checkpoint at their next stage boundary and park; raised gates stay human-decidable; resume is a separate audited act; it never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
A tenant at its per-tenant token ceiling produces an explicit unavailability, not a silently truncated answer.
Model output is treated as untrusted input, validated, never executed as commands; guards against prompt injection.
Curation is retained: only approved content enters the coaching corpus; embeddings change how an asset is found, never whether it was approved.
Retrieval is hybrid: a metadata filter narrows the corpus before semantic ranking, so a torque clip cannot surface on a paint screen.
A default is retained: each screen or failure type keeps a curated fallback asset per locale for cold start.
Retrieval quality is evaluated: retrieval behaviour is checked against scenario evaluations from day one, exactly like every other agent capability.
A retired asset with a surviving index entry is a defect of the highest order, because it means a retired asset could be retrieved.
The stub is honest and stays honest: a stubbed inbound endpoint returning 501 must not be quietly upgraded to accept payloads in a patch release.
Reserved external fields are held NULL and mean nothing until activation; they must not be repurposed for any other use in the interim.
The run_source enumeration is complete at four values: manual, auto_scheduled, erp_inbound and api_inbound. At the first version only manual is producible.
An inbound system is a creator; it is never an approver. The Job state machine and the creator-cannot-approve rule bind it exactly as they bind a human.
The usage export carries counts and metadata only, never operational content: no worker name, measurement value, evidence photograph or workflow content.

The usage ladder produces flags, never enforcement: 80 per cent banner, 100 per cent escalation, 100-125 per cent burst tolerance with burst entry recorded, above 125 per cent a flag opening a commercial conversation.
There is no invoicing, no payment execution, and no pricing engine anywhere on the platform.
An item on the exclusion list is answered by citing it, never by re-arguing it; changing an entry is a client scope decision.
No integration failure may reach the deterministic layer. An integration outage is strictly less powerful than an emergency pause, so it cannot do what an emergency pause cannot do.
No integration failure may make an offline device appear remotely controlled or make a command appear applied.
An incident is not closed when the dependency returns; it is closed when the records agree.
Every stored item belongs to exactly one data class; a class's rules are the strictest of any rule that applies; rules are enforced by the store contract rather than by application discipline.

Evidence media is immutable at creation; corrections are append-only annotation records carrying who, when and what changed; the original is never altered; captured media never touches the device gallery.

One append-only audit log per tenant under the one-transaction guarantee, with no delete or edit path on any surface for any role including the Root Super Admin; the audit log is never shorter-lived than the data it evidences.
Memory has no export path on any surface at the first version, and this blueprint proposes none.

Storage is metered as exactly four named dimensions — evidence media, workflow packages, the parts registry, and training content — and training content is metered separately because the Training Library is online-only and excluded from offline packages.
Under the no-purge lifecycle model storage accumulates perpetually; the tiering curve is the cost lever; there is no delete lever at all.
Tenant isolation: no data belonging to one tenant is readable, writable, inferable or countable by any principal acting for another tenant.
business_rules.enforcement_point: identity, authorization, data, storage, analytics, integration, support and audit layers

business_rules.statement: Every request carries a tenant context derived from the session and never from a client-supplied parameter; an access without a tenant constraint fails closed.
There is no degraded mode for isolation; the fallback for a failed isolation check is refusal, not accommodation. A manual override of isolation does not exist and must not be built.

Data residency at the first version is a single stated region in the client's cloud environment, cloud United States region, client-owned account; region-per-tenant is roadmap and no per-tenant control exists.
The retention horizon is a speed promise, not an existence promise. Every surface that displays retention must use horizon language; a screen labelled 'Delete after 15 years' would be false.
Retention-value changes are critical-class, ride maker-checker with root approval, and write to both the platform and the tenant audit trails.
Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it, and the client identifies which standards those are.

Legal hold suspends tiering and any compliance-driven deletion for its scope; place and release are dual-approved critical-class acts, tenant-visible, and audited; an unapproved release leaves the hold in force.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Super Admin Data Lifecycle and Archival

business_rules.statement: Where scope resolution is uncertain, hold wider rather than narrower, because over-preservation is recoverable and under-preservation is not.

Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act: worker personal data anonymises at 24 months for standard tenants; measurement, result and evidence survive; identity becomes a pseudonym; it never happens in Regulated-Industry mode.
Switching a tenant into Regulated mode later does not resurrect anonymised identities — an onboarding conversation, not a surprise.
The opaque worker identifier is stable per worker within a tenant and is not reused across workers.
The anonymisation audit entry records the event without recording the identities, because an audit trail preserving the names would make the irreversible act reversible.
The legal-hold check precedes erasure execution, always. Legal hold outranks erasure; a preservation obligation defeats an erasure request and the requester is told so.
An erasure certificate is written to both audit trails only where deletion actually occurred, and never otherwise.
Erasure cannot destroy audit completeness; erasure inside audit records is identity replacement with the row retained, never removal of an audit row.
Export is a person-initiated act, with one scheduled exception: standard-report delivery, which a person configures and which delivers to people by in-app and email rather than into a system.
An export carries the authority of the person who produced it and can never contain more than its producer could read on screen.
Every export is itself an audited action, recorded with producer, scope and timestamp.

No completeness claim may be made while an open decision remains; no artifact may claim completeness, full compliance, or a coverage percentage while any decision in the consolidated table remains open.

The word 'job' never appears on any of the five surfaces to mean a scheduled work item; the manufacturing Job keeps the term exclusively. Timer-driven work is a scheduled work item with SCHED- and SCHEDRUN- identifiers.

A fired schedule proves nothing alone. Five facts must each be true independently: the moment arrived; an execution attempt started and claimed the occurrence; the attempt finished without unhandled failure; the business effect was written with its audit event in one transaction; and where required the command channel delivered it at the device's next sync.
A scheduled item never grants authority, never becomes the sole protection of a safety control, never deletes, and never publishes past a gate.

Safety wins the primary timing slot: if any part of an element enforces safety, authorisation, qualification, tenant isolation, evidence integrity or audit, its primary classification is the enforcement mechanism, never the assisting sweeper.

A scheduled sweeper may assist with warnings, cleanup, reconciliation or detection. It must never be the only control protecting safety, authorization, qualification, tenant isolation, evidence or audit.

Never invent a cadence the source does not give. Where the Statement of Work names a mechanism without a period, the period is TBD — Client Decision Required with a named decision, options, recommendation, trade-off and owner.
Prohibition 1 — a schedule never replaces an action-time check. A missed expiry sweep must never leave an unauthorized action permitted.
Prohibition 2 — a schedule never grants. It may never grant a qualification, extend a clearance, or bypass action-time validation.
Prohibition 3 — publication is event-driven and gated. A scheduled publication must never bypass review, approval, specification, evaluation, signing, packaging or version-pinning gates.
Prohibition 4 — the Frontline application runs no central server scheduled work while offline; only local signed evaluations run on the device.

Prohibition 5 — a notification is never the business action. Creation, sending, delivery, reading or acknowledgement must never automatically mean approval, hold release, publication, qualification, command completion, device application or business-action completion.
Prohibition 6 — scheduled AI output stays advisory or derived. It never executes a state change on its own, never self-approves, never classifies a deviation, and never releases a hold.

Prohibition 7 — retention is never an unconditional deletion timer. Legal hold, evidence integrity, privacy, tenant isolation, audit immutability and approved retention policy are all checked before any deletion, archival, redaction or pseudonymisation.
Prohibition 8 — unsynchronised Frontline evidence and local audit records are never deleted on age alone. Eviction follows confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check.
In-app notifications cannot be muted and are one of exactly two notification channels; the only channels anywhere in the platform are in-app and email.

The Severity 1 floor is automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation; the freeze is placed locally and immediately on the device while only escalation delivery waits for connectivity.
Every value not present in the Statement of Work is marked TBD — Client Decision Required with an owner; inventing one would create a false contractual commitment.
business_rules.applies_to: timeouts, retries, rate limits, RTO/RPO, cadences

decisions.question: Should a valid assertion for an unknown subject create a user record automatically (just-in-time provisioning on first assertion)?
options: (a) refuse sign-in for unknown subjects
(b) create a record with no roles
(c) create a record with a tenant-configured default role
decisions.adopted_working_position: option (a) refuse sign-in for unknown subjects, the interpretation this blueprint adopts pending the decision
decisions.impact: Onboarding friction versus letting an external system create platform identities

decisions.question: What are the integration timeout, retry, rate-limit and circuit-breaker parameters?
options: set per integration in the Observability and Integrations setting categories with platform floors and ceilings
fix them platform-wide
decisions.impact: Determines how a partial outage feels and how much load lands on a struggling third party

decisions.question: What is the external processor status of the embedding service for coaching media containing identifiable workers?
options: (a) contract the embedding provision with a no-retention, no-training commitment and disclose the processor
(b) apply personal-data redaction before embedding
(c) run the embedding model inside the client's own cloud environment
decisions.adopted_working_position: option (a), the interpretation this blueprint assumes pending a decision
decisions.impact: Launch tenant information-security and works-council review; GDPR deferred at first version

decisions.question: What is the meaning and producer of the api_inbound run source?
options: (a) reserved for a future general inbound API, unusable at the first version
(b) a synonym reserved for integrator-mediated inbound traffic
(c) the value is removed as premature
decisions.adopted_working_position: recommendation is option (a), documented as reserved and unusable
decisions.impact: An enumeration value with no producer is dead scaffolding or an unstated API commitment

decisions.question: What is the mechanism of the usage-ledger export — operator-initiated console file or an automated outbound feed?
options: (a) operator-initiated console export only at the first version
(b) operator-initiated export plus a scheduled drop to a client-controlled destination
(c) a full machine-to-machine feed
decisions.impact: An automated feed is a new outbound integration with credential, schedule, retry and failure mode

decisions.question: What are the Recovery Time Objectives and Recovery Point Objectives, per data class and per integration?
options: (a) a single platform-wide pair
(b) a pair per data class from section 45.11
(c) a pair per tenant tier
decisions.impact: Determines backup frequency, replication topology and infrastructure cost

decisions.question: What is the named region, and what are the processing locations of the three third-party processors?
options: (a) name the region and publish a processor list with locations
(b) name the region only, processor locations commercially confidential
(c) defer both until a tenant asks
decisions.impact: A single stated region is only an assurance once the region is actually stated

decisions.question: Does a legal hold suspend 24-month personal-data anonymisation?
options: (a) a hold suspends anonymisation for its scope
(b) anonymisation proceeds regardless
(c) the hold object carries an explicit flag chosen at placement
decisions.impact: A preservation order could silently produce unattributable records, and anonymisation is irreversible

decisions.question: How does erasure interact with the append-only audit log?
options: (a) audit rows never altered, erasure limited to non-audit classes
(b) audit rows undergo the same identity-replacement transformation
(c) identity replaced plus a tombstone appended recording that a transformation occurred
decisions.adopted_working_position: Rule five treats option (b) as the working interpretation; recommendation is option (c)
decisions.impact: Audit immutability and right-to-erasure structurally conflict; one obligation must yield

decisions.question: Which compliance standards mandate deletion — the no-purge model's one dependency?
options: (a) the client supplies a named list
(b) the client states that no applicable standard mandates deletion at the first version
(c) the question is deferred, which is the current state
decisions.status: open — already in the canon register
decisions.impact: The deletion exception has no trigger; leaves an unbounded obligation

decisions.question: What is the archived-data retrieval expectation — minutes, hours, or next business day?
options: (a) minutes, implying a warm archive tier
(b) hours, implying a standard archive tier
(c) next business day, implying a deep archive tier
decisions.status: open — already in the canon register
decisions.impact: Drives the archive-tier technology choice and is very expensive to change after data is written

decisions.question: Confirmation that 24-month anonymisation stands unchanged under the no-purge model.
options: (a) confirm as presumed — anonymisation stands, being a transformation and not a purge
(b) retain identities for the full horizon for all tenants
(c) make the 24-month period tenant-configurable within platform bounds
decisions.adopted_working_position: marked in the source as a drafting item, presumed yes; recommendation is option (a)
decisions.status: open — already in the canon register
decisions.impact: No-purge claims nothing ceases to exist while anonymisation permanently destroys a category of information

decisions.question: Does soft suspension release on payment or on an explicit operator signal, given there is no payment integration?
options: release on payment event
release by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console
decisions.adopted_working_position: release by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console [Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14]
decisions.status: adopted working position, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: If release were automatic on payment, a payment-event integration would have to exist; it does not

decisions.question: Is the Prevention Agent action-gated at runtime or bound by authoring-time pre-authorised policy?
options: §3.7 and §6.6.1 pre-authorised policy with a runtime gate only beyond it

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The fallback router role, then the lightweight router role where the capability tolerates reduced capability
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: All router roles unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Honest agent unavailability with a reason category; the deterministic backbone runs untouched; gates raised before the outage remain human-decidable; the floor continues to execute, classify and hold
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Checkpointed orchestrator runs resume at stage boundaries; resume is a separate audited act where an emergency pause was involved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Provider outage, unsupported or oversized asset, index write failure, model-version incomparability, empty filtered set
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Serve retrieval from the existing index while indexing is paused, stated clearly in the Studio as Indexing unavailable
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The index itself is unreadable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Curated default asset per screen and locale; if none, no coaching rendered and the omission recorded; the worker proceeds with the authored work instruction and deterministic gates continue to apply
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The re-index queue drains in submission order when the provider returns

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Stub unreachable, excessive inbound traffic, a caller misreading 501 as transient and retrying aggressively
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Manual run creation in the Delivery Operations Hub, which is the standard operating mode
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — manual creation is already the manual path and there is nothing beneath it
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform operates exactly as designed with no inbound integration at all, which is the first version's intended state
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not applicable at the first version — nothing to recover

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Export generation failure, coverage gap for a period, unattributable re-derivation difference, double export
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-generate the export
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The export cannot be generated at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Usage data is complete and readable in the console even if no export can be produced; billing is delayed and no factory is affected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-derivation from source events, always possible because the ledger is event-sourced

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A query missing its tenant constraint, a tenant identifier accepted from a caller, a shared cache serving one tenant's entry to another, agent context assembled across tenants, an aggregate small enough to identify a single tenant, a mirrored audit event written to the wrong tenant
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deny and audit — there is no degraded mode for isolation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — a manual override of isolation does not exist and must not be built
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected capability is disabled platform-wide until the defect is corrected; data that crossed is treated as disclosed and reported, not quietly deleted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correction plus a full re-run of the cross-tenant negative-test suite

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The tiering scheduler fails to run, a run partially completes leaving data in neither place, archived data cannot be retrieved, a retention change is applied without approval, hot storage fills
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-run the tiering scheduler; failed items remain hot, which is a cost consequence and never a data-loss consequence
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Archive retrieval fails — the data is not lost, it is unavailable, and the incident is a retrieval incident
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: All data remains hot and nothing tiers, which costs money and preserves every guarantee; a tiering system should fail towards keeping data expensive and available
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-run and re-reconcile; volume-out equals volume-in per tenant per class

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The scope resolves incompletely, the tiering scheduler ignores the exclusion, a hold is released without approval, a hold is placed but not visible to the tenant
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Where scope resolution is uncertain, hold wider rather than narrower
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Suspend the tiering scheduler entirely for the affected tenant; then platform-wide
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No data moves anywhere, for anyone, until holds can be honoured. This is expensive and correct.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correct the scope, re-reconcile, and disclose any item that moved; escalation goes to the client's legal function immediately

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The scheduler anonymises a Regulated-Industry-mode tenant, the opaque identifier is unstable, anonymisation partially completes, the event runs without being surfaced first, an anonymisation touches a measurement, result or evidence value
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Halt the scheduler on any pre-run policy assertion failure — there is deliberately no continue-and-fix-later, because there is no later
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Suspend anonymisation platform-wide until the defect is corrected
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No anonymisation runs at all and identities are retained beyond 24 months; retaining an identity too long can be corrected, anonymising too early cannot
failures_fallbacks.recovery: For a deferred event, correct and re-run. For an incorrectly executed one there is no recovery — only disclosure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Scope resolution misses a class, the hold check is bypassed, execution partially completes, a certificate is written where no deletion occurred, an erasure removes an audit row
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Halt the workflow at the first failed check and record the halt
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Suspend the erasure capability and answer requests manually with a written outcome
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No erasure executes, requests queue with their state visible, requesters are told the truth about the delay, and nothing is destroyed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correct the scope resolver and re-run; where over-execution occurred there is no technical recovery and disclosure is the only path

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Export generation fails, an export exceeds a practical size, an export contains data outside the producer's access scope, a PDF render omits a section, a scheduled report fails to deliver
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the generation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Read the data on screen, which is always possible because every export corresponds to a surface the producer can already see
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No export is produced and the data remains readable in the platform; an audit is inconvenienced, nothing is lost or exposed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-generation; producing an export whose scope assertion failed is blocked under all conditions

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Loss of the scheduling control plane: no occurrence becomes due and every timer goes quiet at once
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A standby controller in the same region takes the lease and resumes from durable occurrence rows, with misfires recorded rather than skipped
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual governed triggering by a named platform operator under reason capture and audit is also unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Scheduler stopped, business state unchanged, nothing silently expired: runs stay complete past their window rather than being closed by guesswork, clearances stay valid until the device evaluates them locally
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resumption of the controller plus a bounded, authorised backfill of the missed window

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A mis-assignment: an element that enforces something is given a scheduled primary classification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Rejection of the row and reassignment under the four binding rules
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The reviewer cannot agree on the primary; record the element as TC-13 with a DEC- identifier rather than picking one
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The element is implemented with its enforcement at action time and no sweep at all
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-run of the pass over the affected family; reconciliation is a completeness count

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Register drift: the platform runs a schedule the register does not describe, or the register describes one that does not run
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Raise the difference as a defect against a named owner
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The owner cannot resolve it; disable the undocumented schedule rather than document it retrospectively
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No undocumented schedule runs, accepting the loss of whatever the schedule did
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Authoring the row and the card, passing the approval path, and re-enabling

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A control from the Do-Not-Use-Cron register being implemented, or later refactored, as a scheduled sweep
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Block the change at review
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A scheduled implementation has already shipped; add the action-time or device-local check immediately and leave the sweeper in place as a redundant assist
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The protected action is refused rather than permitted while the correct control is missing
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Removal of the sweeper's authority once the correct control is verified in production

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Value drift: an implemented timer differs from the anchored register value
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Raise a defect and correct the implementation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The difference is a deliberate but unrecorded client instruction; record it as Client Decision Required and preserve both values
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The stricter of the two values applies — stricter is always acceptable, looser is rejected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected register row plus a corrected default; full comparison run per environment

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An incomplete sweep: a candidate group closed while a candidate remains unclassified
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reopen the group
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The source genuinely does not support a decision; record the candidate as TC-13 with a decision identifier
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The candidate is not implemented, because an unclassified timer is an unreviewed timer
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-sweep after the decision lands; reconciliation is a count of candidates against classifications per group

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A prohibition violated in production, most plausibly by a refactor moving a check out of a request path into a background pass
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Revert the change
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The change cannot be reverted because dependent work has shipped; restore the action-time check while leaving the background pass in place with its authority removed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The protected action is refused for everyone until the correct control is verified, accepting an operational stoppage in preference to an unauthorised action
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Verification in production and re-enablement; review every action taken in the affected window against the authority that should have applied

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Chapter-level integration surface drift: an unrecorded external dependency enters the running platform
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Record the drift as a defect and either remove the dependency or promote it to a full card with a client decision
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A dependency that cannot be removed without breaking a shipped behaviour, which means an unapproved integration is load-bearing
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected behaviour is disabled rather than the unapproved dependency being retrospectively blessed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The ordinary scope path in the chapter workflow; reconciliation compares inventory, egress allow-list and platform audit log

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Data misclassification: an item governed by the wrong class, producing the wrong retention, export exposure or erasure behaviour
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reclassification and re-application of the class rules
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Data has already been exported under the wrong class, e.g. operational content reaching the usage export
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected export is withdrawn and the recipients notified, because an isolation or content-boundary breach outranks controlled continuity
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reclassification plus a corrected export; reconciliation is the periodic export-content scan

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Meter drift: a storage dimension's measured volume diverges from the actual stored volume
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-derivation, available because the ledger is event-sourced
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The store's own reporting is also unreliable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The client is told the cost telemetry is unreliable for the affected dimension rather than shown a number that is wrong
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected meter plus re-derivation of affected periods

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A residency assertion the platform cannot honour, most likely a commercial commitment the single-region architecture cannot meet
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Withdraw the assertion and offer the recorded position
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A tenant has already been onboarded under the assertion
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant is told the true position and offered offboarding with export-on-archival at no charge
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Either a roadmap delivery of region-per-tenant, scoped and costed, or an agreed variation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Exclusion erosion: an excluded capability appears in the product without a scope decision
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Removal
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A launch tenant has already come to depend on it
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capability is disabled and the dependency is treated as an escaped scope item requiring a client decision
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A proper scoping; reconciliation compares the shipped feature set against the exclusion matrix at each release

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A failure and fallback matrix row that is wrong: the stated first fallback does not actually engage
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Correct the row
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The behaviour cannot be made to match the row within the release
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The row is corrected to describe the true behaviour and the gap is recorded as a risk, because a matrix describing an aspiration is worse than one describing an unsatisfactory reality
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The engineering work; reconciliation is the fault-injection suite re-run each release
